cards.name: Fixed 60 Hz simulation step with clamped delta
cards.summary: Each update measures real elapsed time, clamps it to between one and two 60 Hz frame periods, then scales it by two global rates; a disabled clock freezes game time
cards.behavior: Each update reads the hardware tick counter and converts the elapsed ticks to seconds. That delta is clamped to at least one 60 Hz frame period (1/60 s) and at most two (1/30 s), so game time never advances by less than a frame per update. The clamped value is stored as the real delta. The scaled delta is the clamped value times a global rate and a power-up rate, both 1.0 by default, and it is zero when the clock is disabled. Game time advances by the scaled delta. When the scaled delta is at least one frame period, it also replaces the stored real delta, so effects that read the real delta follow the slowed or sped-up pace. A separate real-time clock advances by the stored real delta.

constants.name: Fixed simulation frame rate
constants.unit: frames per second, the frame period used for the delta clamp

constants.name: Maximum delta clamp
constants.unit: frame periods (2 x 1/60 s = 1/30 s upper bound per update)

constants.name: Default global time scale
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier of the clamped delta, default for both global rates

cards.name: Scoped camera zoom policy
cards.summary: The scoped look mode zooms between the full field of view and one tenth of it and pulls the near clip in to 49 units while active
cards.behavior: A look policy keeps a stack of up to four look modes; a push beyond four is ignored. Activating the scoped look decomposes the current camera matrix into pan and tilt, resets the tilt to a stored default, clears the pan and tilt speeds and the zoom value and speed, and sets the field-of-view limits to the camera base field of view divided by a maximum zoom factor of 10 at the narrow end and the full base value at the wide end. It also saves the current near clip value in a field whose purpose is not named, then sets the near clip to 49 world units. The init values for a sniper screen fraction (0.5) and a sniper radius (-1) are set at policy creation, and their use is in unrecovered code, so they are only listed here as defaults.

constants.name: Maximum zoom factor
constants.unit: divisor of the base field of view (narrowest view is base divided by 10)

constants.name: Look-mode stack depth
constants.unit: entries; further pushes are ignored

constants.name: Scoped near clip
constants.unit: world units, set when the scoped look activates

constants.name: Default sniper screen fraction
constants.unit: init default of a screen-fraction field, use unverified

constants.name: Unset sniper radius
constants.unit: init default, -1 assumed to mean unset (unverified)

cards.name: Guard vision envelope
cards.summary: Guard detection tests a vertical tolerance and a horizontal range, then a view cone that is wide near the guard and narrows with distance; a latch keeps tracking out to a longer range
cards.behavior: The numbers below are init defaults that other code can overwrite. The detection function is a partial reconstruction (about half of its instructions match) that the default build replaces with assembly, so the order and direction of its checks are approximate. Without an authored exclusion volume, a target is dropped when the vertical gap is over 300 units or the horizontal distance is over the maximum sense range of 2000 units. A new detection also needs the horizontal distance under the outer radius of 1500 units, so a guard that already has the target latched keeps tracking out to 2000 while a fresh detection stops at 1500. The view cone limit is pi radians inside the inner radius of 1000 units and tapers linearly toward pi over 4 at the outer radius. It is compared with an angle from a helper that is not recovered, and in the reconstruction the comparison direction looks inverted, so the cone is the least certain part. A final unrecovered check can still veto the detection. A success sets a latch that stays until a later check fails.

constants.name: Inner detection radius
constants.unit: world units; the cone is widest (pi) inside this horizontal distance

constants.name: Outer detection radius
constants.unit: world units; the cone reaches its narrowest at this horizontal distance and fresh detection stops here

constants.name: Maximum sense range
constants.unit: world units of horizontal distance beyond which a target is dropped

constants.name: Vertical sense tolerance
constants.unit: world units of height difference

constants.name: Outer cone angle divisor
constants.unit: divisor of pi giving the cone angle at the outer radius (pi/4 radians)

capabilities: detection latch with longer keep range

cards.name: Guard attack sector
cards.summary: Guards start with an attack reach of 300 units and an attack angle limit of 60 degrees, and the authored limit is set in degrees and stored in radians
cards.behavior: At init a guard stores a distance field of 300 world units and an angle field of pi over 3 radians (60 degrees). The setter for the attack angle maximum is the only readable use of the angle field: it takes degrees and multiplies by the degrees-to-radians factor, so level data can override the 60 degree default. The name of the 300 unit field is not recovered, so reading it as the attack reach is an inference. The attack test itself is unrecovered assembly.

constants.name: Attack reach
constants.unit: world units, init default of an unnamed distance field (read as attack reach, unverified)

constants.name: Attack sector divisor
constants.unit: divisor of pi giving the default attack angle limit (pi/3 radians, 60 degrees)

constants.name: Degrees-to-radians factor
constants.unit: radians per degree, applied when the attack angle limit is assigned

capabilities: attack angle limit in degrees converted once

cards.name: Alarm network fan-out
cards.summary: An alarm maps three trigger kinds to three alarm states and links to at most 16 sensors, 6 guards and 4 breakable relays
cards.behavior: A trigger call maps the trigger kind to an alarm state: trigger gives the triggered state, untrigger gives the enabled state and disable gives the disabled state, and any other kind is ignored. The new state is applied by a setter that is not part of the readable source. An alarm holds fixed lists of linked sensors (16), guards (6) and breakable relays (4), and level link calls silently ignore additions past each cap. Disabling a breakable relay increments a counter on the alarm. A fourth list of 8 reaction slots is filled through a helper that is not readable here.

constants.name: Sensor links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, list cap

constants.name: Guard links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, list cap

constants.name: Breakable relay links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, list cap

constants.name: Reaction slots per alarm
constants.unit: entries passed as the list capacity to a helper

capabilities: linked sensor, guard and breakable lists

cards.name: Laser beam timing and camera sensor disable latch
cards.summary: A laser beam extends or retracts at a normalized rate of one over the requested duration, sensors keep short trigger filter lists, and a camera sensor disabled right after its alarm stays disabled
cards.behavior: A laser starts with a full draw length of 1.0. Retract stores a normalized rate of minus one over the requested duration and extend stores plus one over it, so the beam would cover its full length in that many seconds; the code that integrates the rate is not readable here. Every sensor keeps up to 4 object ids and 4 classes it should trigger on and up to 4 of each it should ignore, and additions past 4 are ignored. For a camera sensor, disabling it also checks the linked alarm: when the alarm state is disabled and the alarm last changed state within 0.2 seconds (either side), the sensor is marked to remain disabled indefinitely, so a sensor shut off together with its alarm does not re-arm.

constants.name: Beam draw maximum
constants.unit: normalized beam length, 1.0 means full length, init default

constants.name: Object trigger slots
constants.unit: entries per sensor list (object ids and classes, trigger and ignore)

constants.name: Retract rate coefficient
constants.unit: beam length fractions per second per second of requested duration (rate is this value divided by the duration)

constants.name: Extend rate coefficient
constants.unit: beam length fractions per second per second of requested duration (rate is this value divided by the duration)

constants.name: Re-arm suppression window
constants.unit: seconds of game time between the alarm state change and the disable, absolute difference

capabilities: alarm-linked disable latch on camera sensors

cards.name: Coin bounce and collection
cards.summary: Coins start with tuned bounce and collect radii, per-bounce velocity retention, a glint chance and a randomized lifetime window
cards.behavior: Init sets a bounce radius of 45 units, a collect radius of 50 units, a launch speed cap of 250, a last-bounce speed of 50, horizontal and vertical bounce retention factors of 0.6 and 0.75, a glint chance of 0.25 and a lifetime limit range of 8 to 10 seconds. Read from the field names, the radii decide when a coin touches the ground and when it can be collected, each bounce keeps 60 percent of horizontal and 75 percent of vertical speed, and a coin disappears after a lifetime inside the 8 to 10 second range, probably drawn at random. Only the init defaults are shown in readable source; the per-update code that applies them is compiled from unrecovered assembly, so how they are used is inferred from field names.

constants.unit: world units, init default

cards.name: Lucky charm pickup
cards.summary: Charms use a wider bounce and collect radius than coins and keep less vertical speed per bounce; collecting one starts a swirl and a sound
cards.behavior: Init sets both the bounce radius and the collect radius to 60 units, a launch speed cap of 300, a last-bounce speed of 0, horizontal and vertical bounce retention factors of 0.75 and 0.5, and a glint chance of 0.35. Compared with a coin, a charm keeps more horizontal speed (75 percent against 60) and half its vertical speed per bounce, so it hops lower. Collecting a charm switches it to a swirl state, plays a collect sound and sends a splice event to the level object. Only the init defaults are shown in readable source; the per-update code that applies them is compiled from unrecovered assembly, so how they are used is inferred from field names.

cards.name: Key pickup and persistence
cards.summary: Keys use a 35 unit bounce and collect radius, a high launch speed cap and a 0.75 glint chance, and start removed when the level state says they were already collected
cards.behavior: Init sets both radii to 35 units, a launch speed cap of 500, a last-bounce speed of 250, horizontal and vertical bounce retention factors of 0.6 each and a glint chance of 0.75. If the current level state has its key-collected flag set at init, the key starts in the removed state so it cannot be picked up twice. cards.name: Breakable prop shard lifecycle
cards.summary: Breakables carry a break-cause bit mask (default player contact plus bomb, fragile variant player only); shard pieces go pending on a break message and start fading after one static frame or a lifetime
cards.behavior: A breakable keeps a bit mask of what can destroy it. Bit 0 is break-on-player and bit 2 is break-on-bomb, so the default mask of 5 accepts both and the fragile variant mask of 1 accepts player contact only. A break message sets a shard piece to the pending state. A pending piece changes to fading when it has been static for more than one frame, or when its maximum lifetime has passed since entering pending. Entering fading starts a fade-out with a per-piece duration. The default breakable stores a coin count of -1 at init, which is a sentinel whose use is not readable here.

constants.name: Shard pending delay
constants.unit: frames of being static that a pending piece must exceed (1 means more than one frame)

constants.name: Default break cause mask
constants.unit: bit flags, bit 0 player contact and bit 2 bomb

constants.name: Default coin payout
constants.unit: coin count, -1 sentinel meaning unspecified (use unverified)

constants.name: Fragile break cause mask
constants.unit: bit flags, bit 0 player contact only

cards.name: Predictive banking into turns
cards.summary: The banking animation layer starts at full lean strength with a 0.25 second look-ahead interval
cards.behavior: Init gives the banking layer a lean strength of 1.0 and a prediction interval of 0.25 seconds. The function that turns them into a rotation goal is unrecovered assembly, so the described effect, a lean into a turn computed from motion 0.25 seconds ahead, is inferred from the field names.

constants.name: Bank strength
constants.unit: dimensionless lean multiplier, init default

constants.name: Bank prediction interval
constants.unit: seconds of game time ahead, init default

cards.name: Missile target-lead prediction
cards.summary: Missiles reuse the bomb base with trajectory following switched on, a half-second target prediction ceiling and a timed bomb fuse
cards.behavior: Missile init runs the bomb init and sets a follow-trajectory flag to 1. A global holds a maximum target prediction time of 0.5 seconds, which by its name caps how far ahead a missile extrapolates a moving target; the guidance code using it is not readable here. Priming a bomb stores a detonation time equal to the current game time plus the requested fuse.

constants.name: Target prediction horizon
constants.unit: seconds of game time, global default

constants.name: Trajectory-following flag
constants.unit: boolean flag set at init
